goal: Learned Identity Memory Integration into InterMOT
central_question: Does the N72R18 learned identity memory, initialized once by a human correction, improve future public-ID association in the existing InterMOT runtime when candidate generation, assignment solver, public-ID authority, and interaction protocol are held fixed?

encoder.n72r20_candidate_stream: same OSNetEncoder implementation via machine-box crop pipeline

preprocessing.n72r18: machine crop: RGB, /255, bilinear resize to 256x128, ImageNet mean/std
preprocessing.n72r20_candidate_stream: same RGB crop, /255, bilinear resize to 256x128, ImageNet mean/std

feature_dtype.n72r20_candidate_stream: float16 on disk, promoted to float32 before model arithmetic
feature_dtype.risk: The tape is quantized to float16 for storage; report this provenance and do not mix it with an unquantized baseline without using the same tape.

learned_memory.contract: score current observation against current state, then update state; current-frame write is visible only from the next frame

caveats: N72R18 was trained/evaluated on frozen feature caches; this audit establishes feature-space compatibility, not scientific transfer success.
The two current real-SAM3 candidate tapes are train development assets only; no val conclusion is authorized from them.
The identity memory checkpoint is frozen for N72R20 and must not be retrained or selected using association results.
